Special Rules Of Procedure Of The National Assembly
Special Rules Of Procedure Of The National
Assembly
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, 5th June 1962]
No. F. 10-1/62-Legis. Whereas, by Article 231 of the Constitution
it is provided that until rules of its
procedure are made by the National Assembly, the procedure of the Assembly
shall be regulated by rules of procedure made by the President ;
And whereas, the President has
made the requisite rules of procedure ;
And whereas, under the
Constitution, the Speaker or a Deputy Speaker elected by a previous Assembly
remains in office until its successor Assembly has elected its own Speaker and
Deputy Speakers ;
And whereas, there being no
Assembly under the Constitution pre vious to the Commencing Day of the
Constitution, there will be no Speaker or Deputy Speaker to preside over the
Assembly until a Speaker has been elected by the Assembly ;
And
whereas, it is necessary to make provision for the conduct of the meetings
of the Assembly beginning on the Commencing Day, until an elected Speaker takes
the Chair ;
And
whereas, it will take the Assembly some time before the Standing Committees and
other sub-organs of the Assembly are established by the Assembly, and there is
need for making provision for the functions of the Assembly to be performed
during the period before those sub-organs are established';
And
whereas, it will take the President some time before his Council of Ministers
and Parliamentary Secretaries are appointed, and there is need to make
provision in respect of the functions that a Minister or a Parliamentary
Secretary has to perform in relation to proceedings in the Assembly during the
period before such a Minister or Parliamentary Secretary is appointed ;
Now,
therefore, the President is pleased to make the following special rules of procedure,
to provide for the aforesaid contingencies :‑
1.
The duties and functions of the Speaker under the Rules of Pro cedure of the
National Assembly, made by the President in pursuance of Article 231 of the
Constitution, shall, until a Speaker is duly elected by the Assembly, be
performed by the Chief Election Commissioner.
2.
In the aforesaid Rules, those rules that relate to functions of a Standing
Committee or any other sub-organ of the Assembly, and those rules that relate
to functions of a Minister or a Parliamentary Secretary in relation to
proceedings in the Assembly, shall remain inoperative and may be dispensed with
till such times as that Committee or sub-organ is constituted by the Assembly,
or that a Minister or Parliamentary Secretary is appointed by the President.
3.
The programme of the meetings of the National
Assembly up to the introduction of the Budget shall be as given in the Annex.
ANNEXURE
PROGRAMME OF THE MEETINGS OF THE
NATIONAL ASSEMBLY UP TO THE INTRODUCTION OF THE BUDGET
8-6-62.
(Friday)
8 a. m. The Members assemble in Ayub Hall. The Secretary arranges for their seating
alphabetically.
8-15
a.m The Chief Election Commissioner arrives and is
received by the Secretary who conducts him into the Chamber.
8-17 a.m. The Chief Election Commissioner takes the Chair and calls the meeting to
order.
Distribution of the Oath Forms.
8-30 a.m. The President is received by the Secretary who conducts him into the
Chamber.
8-35
a m. Recitation from the Holy Quran.
8-40
a m. The President delivers his address to the Members
of the Assembly.
9 a.m. The President leaves.
The
Chair declares a recess for 5 minutes. (The Members remain in their places).
The
Chief Election Commissioner and Secretary escort the President to his car.
9-05 a.m. The Chief Election Commissioner and the Secretary take their places in
the Hall.
The
Chief Election Commissioner administers the Oath to the Members in groups in
Bengali, Urdu and English as the Members may desire. (Each group of the Mem bers,
standing in their places, repeat the parts of the Oath
